title: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider
hookLine: the Provider, of food, work, friends, faith
tomorrow: the owner finally answers. it's a no. or is it?
last: HE CREATES · HE BRINGS FORTH · SHAPED BY HIM

cards: A grocery receipt is a list of provisions, and nobody reads it twice. Yesterday's question was where to start counting, and Dadi Fatima had an answer before Amira finished asking: start with breakfast. Then who drove you.
Then who answered your text. Dadi's been doing this out loud at the kitchen table for as long as Amira can remember, and today's name is what she's pointing at.

teach.b: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider. The Qur'an says it with a kind of emphasis, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unshakeable might."
And it reaches past people: "And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah." The birds are the picture the Prophet, peace be upon him, used.
In paraphrase from Tirmidhi: if you relied on Allah as He should be relied on, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds.
They go out hungry in the morning and come back full in the evening. Notice the birds still fly out. Provision and effort go together, like the tied camel.
And provision is wider than food. Work is provision. A friend who shows up is provision.
Faith itself, for the one who has it, is counted among His gifts. This week's names fit together here.

The Creator planned; the Maker brought forth; the Fashioner shaped; the Forgiving kept the door open; nothing prevailed over Him; the Bestower gave freely. The Provider keeps it coming, day after day, mostly unnoticed.
One to tell a friend tonight: in the hadith, the birds don't stay in the nest waiting. They go out hungry and come back full.

how: Muslims thank Allah for provision with words like alhamdulillah after meals, and some families name their blessings aloud at the table, as Dadi does.

o: the One who feeds only those who pray
the One who rewards hard work with riches
the One who gives every creature its provision

s: trusting the Provider means you don't need to go out and work
the birds in the hadith go out hungry and come back full. effort and trust together.
in the Qur'an, provision reaches every creature, not only people
there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah.

games.q: this week's review: a friend asks which name fits a free gift with no strings attached. which one?
o: al-Qahhar, the Subduer: nothing prevails over him.
al-Musawwir, the Fashioner: shaped by him.
games.why: al-Wahhab gives without asking a return. the Subduer is the one nothing prevails over; the Fashioner gives each thing its form.

practice: Do Dadi's count. Start with what you ate today, then who helped you get where you are, then one friend, then one thing you were taught. Touch a finger for each one, and when the fingers run out, start again on the first hand.

wordCard.voice: Ar-Razzaq: the Provider, of food, work, friends and faith, for every creature down to the birds.

orig.note: Arabic: the Provider, the One who gives provision (rizq).

carryVoice: The line for today: he provides, and the birds still fly out to find it. A week of names, held.
